title: Half the kit isn't thin: 1,234 lines of doctrine live in Claude adapters with no shared workflow and no Codex equivalent
body:
The kit's stated design is a **thin compatibility layer per runtime** over one
shared workflow: the doctrine lives in `docs/agentic-dev-kit/workflows/`, and each
runtime gets a small adapter that says "read that and follow it". Nothing is
duplicated, so nothing can drift apart.

Four workflows do this. Four do not, and the gap is not small.

| workflow | shared doc | Claude adapter | Codex skill |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session-start` | yes | 8 lines, pointer | 13 lines, pointer |
| `wrap-up` | yes | 8 lines, pointer | 13 lines, pointer |
| `pr-watch` | yes | 9 lines, pointer | 13 lines, pointer |
| `parallel` | yes | 9 lines, pointer | 14 lines, pointer |
| `adopt` | **no** | **116 lines of content** | **absent** |
| `upgrade` | **no** | **197 lines** | **absent** |
| `post-merge-systemize` | **no** | **421 lines** | **absent** |
| `triage-friction-log` | **no** | **500 lines** | **absent** |

**1,234 lines of doctrine live inside `.claude/commands/`** with no shared
workflow behind them.

The `docs/agentic-dev-kit/workflows` string does appear once each in `adopt.md`
and `upgrade.md`, so a grep for it reads as a false positive. Both are mentions of
the *directory as something to install or refresh* —
`adopt.md:72` *"Shared workflows → `docs/agentic-dev-kit/workflows/`"* and
`upgrade.md:162` *"Shared workflows (`docs/agentic-dev-kit/workflows/`) — same
state logic as engines"* — not pointers to their own procedure. Their procedure is
the other 116 and 197 lines.

## Three consequences

**1. Codex can run half the kit, by omission rather than decision.** There is no
`.agents/skills/` entry for any of the four, and no shared doc for one to point at
if there were. A Codex session can start work, hand it off, watch a PR, and run
lanes — and cannot adopt the kit, upgrade it, graduate the friction log, or run
the post-merge retro. Nothing states this limitation; it is visible only by
listing both directories.

**2. Those 1,234 lines are frozen at install time.** No `.claude/` or `.agents/`
path is in `KIT_OWNED` — `kit-manifest.json` tracks 32 files and none is an
adapter. So `/upgrade` never refreshes them and `kit_doctor` cannot report them as
`differs`. An adopter who installed `/triage-friction-log` at an early version
keeps that version permanently, silently, while every engine and shared workflow
around it moves. That is `#37`'s failure mode at four times the size of anything
`#37` covered.

**3. It is why `#236` looked intractable.** On cs-toolkit, `triage-friction-log`
(304 lines) and `post-merge-systemize` (260 lines) are adapter-versus-adapter
comparisons with **no shared doc on either side** to reconcile against. There is
nothing to point the adopter's version *at*, so "convert the fork to a pointer"
has no target.

## Why fixing this collapses #236's design problem

`#236` has been looking for a way to tell "the adopter's own command" from "a
stale copy of a kit command". A slug match was proposed and holed immediately by
the Codex case, where the slugs differ (`session-wrap-up` vs `wrap-up`).

If thin is the rule, that question has a mechanical answer, because **a kit
adapter is derivable rather than authored**: its content is a function of the
slug, the description, and the workflow path. So the upgrade does not need to
track adapters or reconcile them — it can **render** the expected adapter and
compare:

- **Matches the rendered form** → it is a kit adapter. Refresh it freely; nothing
  is lost, because nothing was authored.
- **Does not match** → it is the adopter's own. Leave it, and report that a kit
  workflow of the same name exists whose content is not being read.

The slug mismatch then stops being a duplicate-install hazard and becomes a
**rename to propose**. And no adapter needs to enter `KIT_OWNED`, which is what
made manifest-tracking them unattractive: an adopter like cs-toolkit has 60+ of
its own commands that would all report as `unknown`.

That only works for a workflow that *has* a shared doc. Hence this is a
precondition for the adapter half of `#236`, not a parallel nicety.

## Scope note, because this is four separate jobs

Extracting `triage-friction-log` (500 lines) and `post-merge-systemize` (421) is
not the same size of task as `adopt` (116) and `upgrade` (197), and the two large
ones are also the two where cs-toolkit has a diverged version to reconcile against
afterwards. Worth doing as four changes, smallest first, rather than one sweep —
and worth checking per workflow whether the content is genuinely runtime-neutral
before extracting it, since some of it may be Claude-specific for real reasons
(subagent delegation, `Agent`-tool phrasing) and should stay in the adapter by
design rather than by accident.

Related: `#236` (the upgrade path this blocks), `#93` (the Codex slug mismatch,
one instance of consequence 3), `#37` (untracked kit files never refreshed —
same class, smaller), `#18` (the ownership axis), `#47` (deriving `KIT_OWNED`
from the shipped tree).
